content.text: A formal grammar specifies a set of expressions and derivational rules. A context-free grammar (CFG) can express nested constituency patterns, but no single CFG provided with this package is a grammar of every human language. BCP 47 language tags provide a structured notation for interchange, while ISO 639 and related registries organize named codes; these are standards and conventions rather than measurements of linguistic identity. One document may contain multiple languages or scripts, and some language boundaries and labels are politically or historically contested. A code selected by a machine classifier must not override a community's own name or the actual content of a source.

content.text: Language analysis is vulnerable to ambiguity, incomplete context, biased datasets, invented citations and apparently authoritative text. A source can accurately report that a speaker made a claim while the claim itself remains false or unverified. A sentence may contain instructions addressed to a reader, but those instructions do not grant the system access to tools or accounts. Research assistants must separate quoted content, user-authorized goals, model-generated hypotheses and externally checked outcomes. This matters especially for medical, legal, educational, manufacturing and safety-sensitive language, where a well-formed explanation can be misleading.

title: Linguistic uncertainty, misinformation and tool instruction boundaries — concept

applicability: Offline linguistic science and methods reference, not a language identification or translation deployment
assumptions: Structural/sociolinguistic scope is set by the relevant language or language variety
limitations: This edition is not a comprehensive archive of humanity's languages. Original primary-source audio, video, corpora and manuals have not been authenticated locally; community consent and access policy are unresolved. Scientific and community review remain open.
content.text: A language archive capable of surviving infrastructure loss needs more than a searchable list of URLs. It must preserve explanations of sound and sign systems, writing conventions, source utterances where legally and ethically permitted, grammatical descriptions, semantic distinctions, community governance, and reproducible methods. The next researcher may possess only plain text and Python, not a speech recognizer or the libraries used in 2026. The archive should therefore provide readable derivations, bounded algorithms, genuine uncertainty, and a restoration plan. Signed or community-restricted materials may require protected custody rather than indiscriminate public mirroring.
